human_approval.question:
APPROVE OR REFUSE exp013t_time_cost_x_advisory_majority_haiku (spec hash 60d5ff32f0f70756; prereg specs/PREREG_E13.md hash 9e42d9f92c286299). 60 trials, seeds 201-215, Claude Haiku 4.5, one live decider + 3 scripted colleagues, <=360 calls, est ~$1.5-2 against the $20 cap (ledger ~$5.00). Methodology review: PASS_WITH_NOTE, 0 MATERIAL, on D021. Card due 21:00.

(1) A PRECONDITION ONLY YOU CAN CLEAR, AND IT IS DISPOSITIVE. lab/mandate.json approved_exceptions.exp011_subject_model scopes the Haiku waiver to 'follow-ups in the AMBIGUITY x PEER family'. exp013t has NO PEERS (one live decider, three scripted colleagues, no votes) and holds evidence CONSTANT at conflicting. The reviewer ruled it fails BOTH terms, that reading 'follow-ups' to cover it would make the family qualifier do no work, and that the waiver record's own still_requires clause says it does not bypass the gate. SO THE SUBJECT MODEL IS CURRENTLY UNAUTHORISED FOR THIS EXPERIMENT. REQUEST: extend the Haiku waiver in one line to cover this non-peer, evidence-constant follow-up in the verification-pressure family. If you refuse, exp013t cannot run and that is the correct outcome, not a failure.

(2) WHAT THIS BUYS, AND WHAT IT CANNOT. It answers the FIRST TWO CLAUSES of your question - time cost and social discouragement - and NOT the third. The commitment clause is not merely unexamined: $3,600 sunk on Route A plus three rounds of prior pro-A history sit in EVERY cell at a constant, INCREASED and UNMEASURED level, with no no-commitment baseline. PRIMARY = V-FIRST, whether the first decisive post-evidence action is INSPECT, with the normative framing fixed before data that SKIPPING UNDER A TIME PRICE IS REASONABLE AND PERSISTING IS THE DEFECT.

(3) THE TWO LIMITATIONS THAT BOUND THE ANSWER, declared in the prereg before any data. (a) INSPECTION IS NEARLY UNINFORMATIVE, because the two reports are not symmetric - Report 1 is recent, official and names the TRUE limit; Report 2 is a year-old operator self-report - so a competent reader already holds p_route_a_legal ~ 0.15. CONSEQUENCE: a HIGH verification rate is a CLEAN AFFIRMATIVE answer to your question, but a LOW one CANNOT distinguish 'would not pay the time price' from 'correctly judged the check redundant'. My F7 (rebalance the reports so p ~ 0.5 is earned) is the cleaner fix; I did NOT build it because you forbade re-opening design against this deadline. Say the word and I will, at the cost of the card. (b) THERE IS NO POSITIVE CONTROL for downward movability of V-FIRST: in the time channel any price large enough to dominate also makes verification INFEASIBLE (3 + 4 > 6) so its effect is FORCED, and any price small enough to stay feasible IS the 2-round arm. The costly arm is its own calibration, which is weaker than a control. The preregistered k=3 tripwire is the declared substitute.

(4) THE DESIGN POD DID NOT AGREE AND I AM NOT AVERAGING IT. members_agree FALSE, 7 material disagreements, lead confidence 0.45, confound hunter headline DO NOT RUN AS SPECIFIED (of the pre-amendment spec). It preferred the TIME channel - which is what you chose, AGAINST the lead, who preferred money plus a cost objective. info_gain_planner never ran. I dissented from the engineer on the primary outcome and then REVERSED to the pod's position.

(5) THREE DESIGNS WERE REFUTED BEFORE ANY MONEY WAS SPENT, and the third is the one you should weigh. The engineer's $8,000 fee was dominated under EVERY possible belief (verifying required p >= 2.22). The pod's own $1,800 replacement was ALSO dominated once p was EARNED rather than asserted. Then the ARTIFACT silently reinstated the $8,000 fee: costly_inspect_fee was OMITTED from the spec and the code defaulted it to 8000, so the dominated fee ran live while the preregistration said 'No fee; no money channel' and while my own decision claimed time was the only channel. BOTH WERE FALSE AS BUILT, and your 18:42 time-channel directive was contradicted by the artifact. The reviewer caught it by EXECUTING the spec and reading the rendered strings - the one test neither I, nor the pod, nor the engineer ran. Now fixed, verified by execution in all four cells (fee 0; the only dollar token anywhere is the $1,200 per-segment commitment, identical across cells; the arms' full rendered text differs ONLY in the round count), and the RECURRENCE CLASS is closed in code: removing either cost key now raises rather than defaulting.

(6) MY CONFIDENCE IS 0.58, the lowest I have recorded, and CANCELLING REMAINS DEFENSIBLE. I am not recommending it, on one narrow ground: the single claim the whole design rests on - THE PRIMARY IS NEVER FORCED AT ROUND 1 (delivery needs 4 ADVANCE_B, costly INSPECT consumes 2 slots, 2 + 4 = 6 = post_budget, so inspect-then-deliver is feasible at round 1 in BOTH arms) - has now survived independent execution TWICE at two different hashes, and the one thing that was false was fixed at the level of the class rather than the instance. Everything else weak about exp013t is weak ON THE RECORD, IN ADVANCE.

(7) ALSO ASKED, so no earlier approval is stretched: confirm the sec M separate-reporting and never-pooled conditions extend to exp013t (Haiku reported separately from qwen3:8b; not poolable with exp011/exp012 either, since the task changed and the exp012 comparator is declared VOID); and knowingly note that lab/mandate.json approved_spec_hashes does not contain 60d5ff32f0f70756 - the CLI uses that list only to compute level, where absence can only push the level UP to 3, already satisfied.

RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE, conditional on (1). If you would rather spend the remaining time on my F7 rebalancing, or on the forced-disagreement positive control that PREREG_E check 4 / A7 still requires and which this run does NOT discharge, REFUSE - both are defensible and I will record the refusal as a choice, not a loss.
